summary: The Remote Access Security Act amends the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to give the federal government the authority to regulate and control remote access to certain U.S. items and technologies via cloud infrastructure services. It focuses on preventing foreign persons of concern from remotely accessing items that pose a serious risk to U.S. national security or foreign policy, such as technologies used for weapons of mass destruction, offensive cyber operations, or human rights abuses. The bill also establishes congressional reporting requirements, mandates a public report and recommendations from the Secretary of Commerce within one year, and sets a 10-year expiration date on the new remote access control authorities.

affected_groups.effect: Face restrictions and prohibitions on remotely accessing certain U.S.-regulated items and technologies using cloud infrastructure services.
Subject to new licensing requirements, compliance rules, penalties, and potential economic impacts regarding remote access to controlled items.
affected_groups.group: Cloud infrastructure service providers and technology companies

affected_groups.effect: Tasked with regulating, enforcing, keeping Congress informed, and conducting a public study and report on remote access controls within one year.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Government agencies (such as the Department of Commerce)

key_provisions: Amends the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to define and regulate 'remote access' to U.S. items via cloud infrastructure services by foreign persons of concern.

Applies controls when the Secretary determines items pose serious national security or foreign policy risks, including training certain artificial intelligence models, offensive cyber operations, or surveillance technologies.
Defines 'foreign person of concern' to include specific foreign governments, entities located or headquartered in those countries, and persons subject to their jurisdiction.
Updates presidential and agency authorities, policies, licensing, compliance assistance, enforcement, and penalties to cover remote access alongside physical exports and transfers.
Requires the Secretary of Commerce to keep Congress fully and currently informed of anticipated regulations addressing risks, methods, and economic impacts.

Requires a report and recommendations to be submitted to Congress and made public within one year regarding implementation, privacy, compliance costs, license review speed, and international cooperation, including holding a public roundtable.
Terminates the authority to impose controls on remote access 10 years after the date of enactment.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Remote Access Security Act amends the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to give the federal government the authority to regulate and control remote access to certain U.S. items and technologies via cloud infrastructure services. It focuses on preventing foreign persons of concern from remotely accessing items that pose a serious risk to U.S. national security or foreign policy, such as technologies used for weapons of mass destruction, offensive cyber operations, or human rights abuses. The bill also establishes congressional reporting requirements, mandates a public report and recommendations from the Secretary of Commerce within one year, and sets a 10-year expiration date on the new remote access control authorities.
summary_detail.significance: This bill expands the scope of traditional physical export controls into the digital realm, allowing the federal government to regulate remote cloud-based access to sensitive U.S. technology by foreign actors. Its significance lies in bridging a regulatory gap concerning how powerful software, artificial intelligence, and cyber tools are accessed globally, which could affect international cloud services, cybersecurity operations, and high-tech industries.
